comparisons.peer_topic: Litigation Outcome for California and First Texas Case Patents
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel prevailed on eight patents in the Northern District of California case with final judgment entered in April 2024, though VLSI appealed one finding; in the first Texas case, the Federal Circuit reversed a $675 million award and sent the $1.5 billion award back for remand, while affirming infringement on that patent.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Intel are involved in patent infringement litigation concerning their semiconductor products. Micron is the defendant in complaints filed by YMTC in the U.S. and China alleging infringement of 3D NAND and DDR5 DRAM patents. Similarly, Intel is the defendant in litigation from VLSI Technology alleging infringement of processor and FPGA patents in U.S. federal courts, with Intel prevailing on eight patents in California but facing appeals and separate proceedings in Texas. Both disclosures highlight the cross-border nature of patent disputes in the semiconductor industry and the specific products targeted (memory/processors vs. fpgas/processors).

sentences.text: The second complaint alleges that eleven U.S. patents are infringed by certain of our 3D NAND and DDR5 DRAM products.
The complaints assert that MTI and MSS infringed three Chinese patents owned by YMTC by importing, selling, offering for sale, and assisting others to sell certain 3D NAND products and SSDs in China.

In October 2017, VLSI Technology LLC (VLSI) filed a complaint against us in the US District Court for the Northern District of California alleging that various Intel FPGA and processor products infringe eight patents VLSI acquired from NXP Semiconductors, N.V. (NXP).
VLSI sought damages, attorneys' fees, costs, and interest.

comparisons.peer_summary: In the Shanghai case, the court found no infringement in October 2023, but VLSI appealed this finding; a Supreme People's Court evidentiary hearing and trial occurred in October and November 2024 respectively, with the appeal remaining pending.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies face patent infringement litigation in Chinese courts. Micron was served with complaints in the Beijing Intellectual Property Court alleging infringement of Chinese patents by its 3D NAND and SSD products. Intel faced a similar case in the Shanghai Intellectual Property Court where it was accused of infringing a patent on core processors; although Intel won on infringement in 2023, the case was appealed to the Supreme People's Court. This comparison highlights the parallel regulatory and legal challenges both U.S. semiconductor firms encounter in China regarding intellectual property rights.

sentences.text: On January 22, 2024, Micron Semiconductor (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. ("MSS") was served with three patent infringement complaints filed by YMTC in Beijing Intellectual Property Court and on February 27, 2024, Micron Technology, Inc. ("MTI") was served with the same complaints.
The complaints assert that MTI and MSS infringed three Chinese patents owned by YMTC by importing, selling, offering for sale, and assisting others to sell certain 3D NAND products and SSDs in China.

In May 2019, VLSI filed a case in Shanghai Intellectual Property Court against Intel (China) Co., Ltd., Intel Trading (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and Intel Products (Chengdu) Co., Ltd. asserting one patent against certain Intel core processors.
The court held a second trial hearing in May 2022, and in October 2023, issued a decision finding no infringement and dismissing all claims.
